Only folks with little marks over their letters seem affected. Choosing the international-text option during manual import fixes it. Can the attachment carry that hint automatically? Our supervisors just double-click it.

report.title: Name spellings break in the roster attachment
report.description: Names with accents look scrambled in the downloaded roster, but they're fine inside SkilletSpan.

report.title: Release 6.8.2 broke the directory download
report.description:
Pretty sure this is a regression from SkilletSpan 6.8.2. We installed that release yesterday, and today the staff-directory CSV opens with Maëvi Dorsen written as MaÃ«vi Dorsen in GridNest. The profile still says Maëvi, so the employee record hasn't changed.

I downloaded it three times because I thought I'd grabbed a bad copy. Same result every time. Our back-office lead can make it readable by selecting UTF-8 in the import dialog, but opening it directly is still wrong. Please roll back whatever changed in 6.8.2; we shouldn't need special import settings just to read our staff list.

report.title: Directory printout adds several empty pages
report.description:
To be clear, accented staff names are NOT corrupted in our CSV downloads. Luréna Vaskel appears correctly in the spreadsheet, with no garbled text, and the names are also correct inside SkilletSpan. That part works fine now.

My issue is with printing the directory directly from the app. A two-page roster produces six pages, and the last four contain nothing except the directory heading. I've checked the preview and those empty pages are already there before it reaches the printer. Can we get a print layout that stops after the last employee?

report.title: Split-shift warning includes the hours between shifts
report.description: SkilletSpan is flagging Lessa's split shift as 12 hours of continuous work. She's scheduled 8am–11am and then 5pm–8pm at our Alder Quay restaurant, with nothing assigned between 11 and 5. That's six hours working and six hours off duty. Our maximum continuous-work setting is eight hours, so neither shift should trigger it. The warning appears to be counting straight from the first start time to the last finish time instead of taking out the gap. If I remove either shift, the warning goes away.

report.title: Lunch and dinner visits treated like one all-day stretch
report.description: Can someone explain the red badge on Pella's Tuesday card? She's on the rota 09:00–12:00, goes home for the afternoon, then comes back 18:00–21:00. The badge says she's doing twelve hours, but she's only here for six. We allow eight in a row. It looks like the empty afternoon is being included as though she never left the kitchen.

report.title: Time away still included
report.description: The too-many-hours notice is counting the whole afternoon someone has free between their morning and evening bookings.

report.title: Did release 4.8.2 break the split-day check?
report.description:
We updated to SkilletSpan 4.8.2 yesterday and I'm blaming that release for the compliance banners we're seeing while preparing next week's rota. I can't prove the timing because this is the first week I've personally handled these bookings since the update.

At our Bramble Lantern site, Oren is booked for prep from 07:00 to 10:00 and dinner service from 17:00 to 21:00. The warning calls that fourteen hours against our ten-hour continuous-work limit. He is actually working seven hours. During those seven hours in the middle he leaves the restaurant, has no duties, and isn't expected to be available. These are two separate entries, not one entry with a meal break attached.

I tried changing the evening booking to finish at 20:00. The number in the warning dropped to thirteen, even though the total time he'd be working would then be six hours. Moving his return time from 17:00 to 18:00 didn't change the warning's number at all. That makes it look like only his earliest arrival and latest departure matter, and the time he spends away isn't being deducted.

Deleting the dinner entry clears the banner, but obviously we need him back for service. Please don't suggest raising our limit to fourteen hours as a workaround; that would let genuinely overlong bookings through too. Is there a way to get the check to recognize the afternoon away without turning it off? We're holding publication until we know which of these banners actually need a rota change.

report.title: Compliance check is fine; printed warnings waste ink
report.description: The split-shift warning works fine now: long off-duty gaps aren't counted as continuous work, and nobody is incorrectly flagged for exceeding the maximum duration. My complaint is the print layout. Legitimate compliance warnings get a huge solid-black background, which eats toner and makes handwritten annotations unreadable. Could we have an outline-only print option?

report.title: Shadow trainees make an uncovered station look fully staffed
report.description:
We caught this while checking Friday dinner coverage at our Copper Ladle location in SkilletSpan. Grill needs two people who can work it independently. We originally had two qualified cooks and two new hires scheduled there, with both new hires marked 'shadow trainee.' The coverage meter was green, which made sense while the cooks were still on the schedule.

Then I took one cook off grill and the other off the shift entirely. The two shadow trainees were the only people left assigned to grill, but the meter stayed green and still showed the requirement as satisfied. Neither of those new hires is allowed to run grill without someone training them. Their shifts are there so we can plan who they follow, not because they can replace the cooks.

I checked the employee records because I thought we'd forgotten to set their training status. Both still say shadow trainee. If I remove their assignments too, the coverage warning finally appears. Putting just the trainees back makes it disappear again, without adding anyone qualified to work the station.

This nearly got published as our final dinner plan. Our shift lead spotted the names, but someone checking only the coverage colors would have assumed we were ready. Please make those trainee assignments visible without treating them as full workers for the station's minimum. We need to see that the learners are attending and also that we're still short two qualified cooks.

report.title: Readiness badge says we're set with only apprentices
report.description: At Thistle Pan, we put beginners on the rota alongside the people teaching them. Tonight I deleted every certified cook's grill slot and left just the beginners, whose profiles have the learning-only designation. The little readiness badge still said we had enough people for service. It seems to treat someone who must be supervised exactly like someone allowed to run grill alone. Those are extra learning places, not replacements for the experienced crew.

report.title: Only learners left, still looks covered
report.description: The station still shows enough coverage when everyone left on it is a shadow trainee and nobody can work it alone.

report.title: Release 6.8.2 seems to have broken trainee coverage
report.description:
I'm blaming the SkilletSpan 6.8.2 update for this: prep turns green with two shadow trainees scheduled and no qualified prep worker. Taking the experienced person off doesn't reduce the covered headcount at all. We can't actually open prep with those two unsupervised.

Our assistant lead says she saw the same thing before we installed 6.8.2, but this is the release where I noticed it, so that's what I've put on the ticket. The training labels are definitely still saved on both profiles. Could you check why those assignments satisfy the staffing requirement?

report.title: Coverage is correct; printed schedule cuts off our footer
report.description:
The staffing coverage meter is working fine for us now. Employees marked shadow trainee do not count as full workers, and removing all independently qualified workers from a station does not leave a green coverage indicator.

My actual issue is printing the weekly schedule. The bottom line of our custom footer gets clipped off, including the closing checklist reminder. It appears in the print preview but not on the paper, even with plenty of blank space below the shift rows. Can we get a little more room for that footer?

report.title: Calendar subscription keeps the old shift times after we edit them
report.description:
Our staff subscribe to their SkilletSpan schedules in their personal calendars. When we change a published shift, the times in SkilletSpan update correctly, but the subscribed calendar event keeps its original start and end times.

Yesterday I moved Nessa's dinner shift at Copper Ladle from 4–10 pm to 5–11 pm. She could see 5–11 in SkilletSpan right away. Her calendar still showed 4–10 this morning, even after she manually refreshed it. Two other people have reported the same thing after I shortened their shifts last week. This isn't a missing shift: the appointment is there, on the right date, attached to the right employee. It's just showing the hours we originally published.

I tried adding a note to Nessa's shift so we could tell whether anything was reaching the calendar connection. Looking at the subscription feed directly, the event now contains the new hours and my note. However, the last-modified value is exactly the same as it was before I made those changes. I'm not a calendar expert, but it looks like the receiving app has no reason to replace the copy it already has.

If I remove the subscription and add it again from scratch, the correct hours appear. Asking everyone to do that whenever a manager adjusts coverage isn't workable, especially across our six kitchens. Staff use these calendars to arrange rides and childcare, so an hour makes a real difference.

Could someone check why an edited shift isn't being marked as updated in the subscription? We'd like existing calendar entries to refresh, rather than needing to tell people to delete and reconnect their schedules.

report.title: Dinner moved, but my phone still says four
report.description: The rota in SkilletSpan says I'm working 5–11 now. The little block in my phone's day planner still says 4–10, which was what my supervisor first posted. I use the automatic link, not something I typed in myself. Pulling down to reload doesn't help. Disconnecting that link and setting it up again brings in the right hours, but the next adjustment gets stuck the same way. Can you make the linked copy follow the rota?

report.title: Connected calendar hours stuck
report.description: My subscribed work calendar still has the original shift hours even though the revised hours are right in SkilletSpan.

report.title: Build 8.14.2 broke calendar updates?
report.description: I'm blaming SkilletSpan build 8.14.2 because that's when I first noticed this. We moved a prep shift from 7–12 to 8–1, and the app shows the new hours while my subscribed calendar keeps 7–12. Refreshing doesn't fix it; reconnecting does. Our floor lead says she also had this happen before that build, so maybe my timing is a coincidence. Either way, published shifts show up initially, but later time changes aren't making it into entries already on our calendars.

report.title: Calendar updates are fine; printed rota logo is stretched
report.description: Our personal calendar subscriptions aren't stale: edited shifts update their start and end times correctly, including ones we changed this morning. My complaint is about the printable weekly rota. The Copper Ladle logo comes out stretched across the whole header instead of keeping its proportions. The schedule itself is readable, but the printout looks awful on the staff noticeboard. Can we preserve the logo's aspect ratio?

report.title: Delegated schedule changes look like the manager made them
report.description:
We need help figuring out who actually changed a shift at our Copperladle Kitchens locations. I was covering for our site manager yesterday using the manager delegation option in SkilletSpan. From my own login, I moved a server's Thursday shift from 4 pm to 6 pm and then shortened another shift by an hour. Both changes saved correctly, so this isn't a problem with the schedule itself.

When we checked the schedule audit log this morning, both entries showed only the manager I was representing. My name wasn't anywhere in the entries, including when we opened the details. That manager was off yesterday and didn't touch the app. The log makes it look like they personally made both changes.

I tried a second change while another supervisor watched, just to rule out someone else having changed the same shift. Same result: the represented manager gets listed as the author, with nothing identifying the person actually doing the work. I wasn't signed into their account or sharing their password; I was using the access they had delegated to me.

We thought this had been addressed in 4.9 because delegated timesheet changes now show both people. I checked one of those entries and can see who performed the action as well as whose authority they used. Schedule changes don't seem to have that same information.

This is becoming awkward when staff ask who changed their hours. We can explain it from memory today, but that won't help us review something a month later. Could the schedule history show the actual editor alongside the manager they were representing?

report.title: Rota history credits the person who was away
report.description: I was covering our site lead's duties through the stand-in access they gave me. I used my own sign-in to move two dinner assignments. In the activity trail, the name beside each change belongs to the site lead, who was on leave. Expanding the rows still gives no clue that I was the one clicking. The equivalent trail for recorded work hours includes both of us, so why does the rota only credit the absent person?

report.title: Can't tell who made the change
report.description: The shift history only names the person being covered for, not whoever used their delegated access.

report.title: Did 5.2.1 break the names on schedule history?
report.description:
Since our move to SkilletSpan 5.2.1, we've noticed a pretty concerning attribution issue. I'm blaming that update because it's when our team first spotted it.

Our assistant supervisor changed Saturday's kitchen shifts using delegated manager access. The schedule audit entries all name the site manager instead, even though that person wasn't working that day. There is no second name or 'performed by' detail anywhere we can find. The assistant was definitely using their own account.

Timesheet history still identifies the person doing the work under delegation. It's just the schedule history that makes the represented manager look like the editor. Can you check whether 5.2.1 caused this?

report.title: Audit authors are fine; weekly view keeps losing my zoom
report.description:
To be clear, delegated schedule edits are NOT showing the wrong author for us. The audit log correctly shows who performed the edit and which manager they were representing, so please don't route this as an attribution issue.

My complaint is that the weekly schedule view forgets my zoom level whenever I leave it to open a staff profile. When I come back, the rows are huge again and I have to zoom out to compare the whole week. Nothing is missing and the changes are saved; I just want the view to remember its display setting.

report.title: Leave balance keeps growing while employee is on unpaid leave
report.description: Could someone check the balance for Nera at our Copper Ladle site? She has approved unpaid leave from June 3 through June 21, but SkilletSpan has added leave hours on both weekly accrual runs since she went out. Our group policy says unpaid-leave days don't earn leave. The absence is definitely approved, not just requested, and the dates look right on her profile. I can adjust the balance manually, but I don't want to keep subtracting hours every week or accidentally take away anything she earned before the leave started.

unlisted_problem.title: Leave accrual does not stop during unpaid leave
unlisted_problem.summary: Employees continue earning leave balance during an unpaid leave interval even when the group's accrual policy excludes those days. The accrual job does not consult approved unpaid-leave records.

report.title: How do I make summer availability expire?
report.description: I'm available every Tuesday and Thursday afternoon until August 28, then my classes start. I can set the weekly pattern in SkilletSpan, but I can't find an end date anywhere. Do I really have to remember to delete it myself in August?

unlisted_problem.title: Recurring availability has no end-date option
unlisted_problem.summary: Employees cannot set a recurring availability pattern that ends on a specified date. Seasonal availability must be removed manually when the season finishes.

report.title: Clock-in works, but my screen reader doesn't tell me
report.description:
Posting this for our accessibility ticket. I use a screen reader with the mobile clock. When I activate Clock In, I don't hear a success message or anything else that tells me the punch went through. A coworker watching my screen said a confirmation banner appeared, so it seems the clock-in itself worked.

I checked Time History afterward and the entry was there. That is currently the only way I can confirm it on my own. It's especially confusing during the morning rush: I can't tell whether I should wait, try the button again, or start work. Please have the app announce the confirmation when it appears rather than requiring me to go looking for the recorded punch.

unlisted_problem.title: Clock-in confirmation is not announced to screen readers
unlisted_problem.summary: The mobile app successfully records a clock-in, but its confirmation banner is not exposed as an accessibility announcement. Screen-reader users cannot tell that the action succeeded without navigating to their time history.

report.title: Printed roster cuts off the station names
report.description: The published schedule looks fine on screen, but our printout chops both “Patio Service — East Counter” and “Patio Service — West Counter” down to the same text. The labels don't wrap, so staff can't tell which counter they're assigned to. We need the full station names on the kitchen noticeboard copy.

unlisted_problem.title: Published schedule printouts clip station labels
unlisted_problem.summary: Long station labels are cut off in printable schedule layouts instead of wrapping. The on-screen schedule shows the full labels, but printed assignments can become ambiguous.

report.title: Closed restaurant missing from old timesheet search
report.description:
We're reviewing last winter's hours for the former Mossgate restaurant, which we archived after it closed. Historical timesheet search no longer lists it in the location selector, and I don't see an option for archived sites.

I temporarily reactivated Mossgate and could immediately find the records. Archived it again and it disappeared from the search again. We'd rather not put a closed restaurant back into the active site list whenever someone needs to answer a payroll question. Is there another way to search its old timesheets without reopening it?

unlisted_problem.title: Archived locations cannot be included in historical search
unlisted_problem.summary: The historical timesheet search excludes archived locations and offers no control to include them. Managers must temporarily reactivate a closed restaurant to inspect its old records.

report.title: Copied closing template has no tasks
report.description: Duplicated our evening close template to make a shorter Sunday version. The station and shift length copied over, but the closing checklist didn't. We only noticed after publishing: every shift made from the new template had zero checklist tasks, while the original still has all nine.

unlisted_problem.title: Shift-template duplication drops attached checklists
unlisted_problem.summary: Duplicating a shift template copies its duration and station but omits its opening or closing checklist. Shifts created from the duplicate therefore have no checklist tasks.

report.title: New profile picture is sideways
report.description: My photo is upright in my phone's gallery and was taken with the phone held vertically. After uploading it to SkilletSpan, my profile shows me sideways. Tried uploading the same picture again and got the same result.

unlisted_problem.title: Employee profile photos rotate after upload
unlisted_problem.summary: Profile photos taken in portrait orientation appear sideways after upload. The image-processing service discards orientation metadata without rotating the underlying image.

report.title: Can't submit 3.6 miles between sites
report.description: I covered lunch at Fernwick and then drove to our Ashmere kitchen for prep. The trip was 3.6 miles, but the mileage reimbursement form rejects that value and asks for a whole number. Our reimbursement policy pays for the actual distance to one decimal place. I don't want to claim 4 miles when I drove 3.6, and entering 3 would short me. Can the form accept the distance we actually traveled?

unlisted_problem.title: Mileage reimbursement entries reject fractional distances
unlisted_problem.summary: Employees recording travel between restaurants can enter only whole distance units for reimbursement. Fractional distances are rejected rather than accepted or rounded under the group's reimbursement policy.

report.title: Sorting stations at one site changes the other site's order
report.description:
We manage two restaurants with very different layouts. At Bellrow, we'd like the schedule columns to run Host, Dining Room, Patio, then Kitchen. At Reedquay, the kitchen assignments need to come first because that's how their shift lead does the briefing.

Yesterday I reordered the stations while working in Bellrow. Today Reedquay's manager asked why I'd rearranged their schedule too. We tried setting Reedquay back, and that also changed Bellrow. Switching the location selector before dragging the stations doesn't seem to make a difference.

These are shared station names, so we don't want to create duplicate stations just to get a different display order. Is there a way to save the ordering separately for each restaurant? Right now we're undoing each other's changes.

unlisted_problem.title: Station ordering cannot differ between locations
unlisted_problem.summary: Reordering stations for one restaurant changes their order throughout the group. The product stores one group-wide display order and does not support site-specific ordering.

report.title: Canceling face unlock leaves login stuck
report.description: If I cancel the biometric prompt in the SkilletSpan mobile app, the sign-in screen stops responding. I can't tap password sign-in or any other control. Closing the app completely and reopening it lets me try again, but I'd expect Cancel to let me use my password instead.

unlisted_problem.title: Mobile sign-in freezes after canceling biometric unlock
unlisted_problem.summary: Canceling the biometric unlock prompt leaves the mobile sign-in screen unresponsive. Employees must restart the app before they can choose password sign-in.
